entities.summary: Andrew of Crete, also known as Andrew of Jerusalem, was an 8th-century bishop, theologian, homilist, and hymnographer. He was born in the 7th century, but the exact date is unknown. He became the bishop of Jerusalem in 730 and served until his death in 740. During his tenure, he played a key role in the Council of Nicaea II, where he contributed to the development of the Eastern Orthodox Church's liturgical music. He also wrote several hymns, including the famous 'Jesus Christ, Holy God,' which is still sung in many Orthodox churches today. Andrew's legacy extends to the Catholic Church, where he is venerated as a saint. He is considered one of the most important figures in the development of Eastern Orthodox liturgical music and hymnography. His contributions have had a lasting impact on the spiritual lives of millions of people around the world. The Eastern Orthodox Church continues to celebrate his feast day on July 8, and his hymns remain an integral part of their liturgical tradition.
